article_title: Modular Ships Mojo 1.0, Locking In Language Stability as Compiler Open-Sourcing Awaits
summary: Well-sourced and substantively accurate across all 6 sources, but two quotes in the body do not match their cited sources' exact wording.

findings.message: The article quotes mojolang.org's v1.0.0 release notes as saying Pointer/UnsafePointer unification comes "with unsafety now marked on individual operations with `unsafe_` prefixes." The source's actual sentence is: "Pointer and UnsafePointer are unified into a single Pointer type, with unsafety now marked on the individual operation instead of on the type as a whole." The `unsafe_` prefix detail is real but appears in the following sentence, not this one -- the article merged and reworded two adjacent sentences into a single quotation.
findings.details: Confirmed by reading sources/2026-08/modular-ships-mojo-10-locking-in-language-stability-as-compiler-open-sourcing-awaits/source-1.html.gz (mojolang.org v1.0.0 release notes) directly.

findings.message: The article quotes The Register as saying the Qualcomm acquisition "raised community concerns about vendor neutrality, particularly on Hacker News, where developers questioned whether Qualcomm's ownership might compromise the platform's vendor-neutral positioning." The Register's article never mentions Hacker News; its actual text reads: "An open source release of the compiler and toolchain would address concerns expressed by some in the development community about Qualcomm's acquisition of Modular, and whether the chip designer's takeover might compromise Modular's commitment to a vendor-neutral AI development platform." The general concern is real; the specific attribution to Hacker News is not supported by the source and appears to be a fabricated detail.
findings.details: Confirmed by reading sources/2026-08/modular-ships-mojo-10-locking-in-language-stability-as-compiler-open-sourcing-awaits/source-4.html.gz (The Register) in full -- 'Hacker News' does not appear anywhere in the article text.

content_preview.title: Modular Ships Mojo 1.0, Locking In Language Stability as Compiler Open-Sourcing Awaits
content_preview.summary: Modular released Mojo 1.0 on August 11, promising API stability and pledging to open-source the compiler in 2026, two months after Qualcomm agreed to buy the company.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Modular released Mojo 1.0 on August 11, 2026, as part of the company's Modular 26.5 update, marking the first stable version of its Python-inspired systems programming language since it debuted in 2023, according to [Linuxiac](https://linuxiac.com/mojo-1-0-programming-language-officially-released/). Announced in a [Modular blog post](https://www.modular.com/blog/modular-26-5-mojo-1-0-is-here) and confirmed the same day on [Modular's official forum](https://forum.modular.com/t/mojo-1...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-organized, thorough News piece covering the release, the stability pledge, technical changes, and the Qualcomm-acquisition context. Genuine follow-up to two prior Machine Herald articles, both verified to resolve.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 6 snapshots directly. Modular's blog (source-0) confirms every quote verbatim ('During the 1.x timeframe...', 'just a language we are developing... every day in production', 'we will open source the Mojo compiler and toolchain in 2026', the roadmap quote). mojolang.org's v1.0.0 release notes (source-1) confirm the lambda and 'all variable declarations should use var' quotes verbatim, but the Pointer/UnsafePointer quote is a reworded merge of two sentences (see finding). Modular's official forum post (source-2) confirms the '200 contributors...200k+ lines...1,000 more...filed issues' quote verbatim, dated Aug 11 2026. mojolang.org's release listing (source-3) confirms all three version dates (v1.0.0 Aug 11, v1.0.0b2 Jun 18, v1.0.0b1 May 7) verbatim. The Register (source-4) confirms the LLVM/Clang/Swift/MLIR creator attribution and the 'unify the AI software stack... diverse set of GPUs, CPUs, ASICs' quote verbatim, but never mentions 'Hacker News' anywhere in the article -- the specific attribution in the submission's quote is not supported by the source (see finding). Linuxiac (source-5) confirms the LSP/memory-safety/Mojo AI Skills claims and the NVIDIA/AMD/Apple hardware-support claim.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: The underlying facts behind both flagged quotes are directionally accurate (pointer unification with unsafe_ prefixes is real; community vendor-neutrality concerns following the Qualcomm deal are real, corroborated independently in the source's Q&A section about Nvidia/AMD). The issue in both cases is that specific wording/details were added or merged into a quotation rather than reproduced verbatim -- not fabrication of the underlying event.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral; the Analysis section is clearly framed as analysis.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate of prior archive coverage -- correctly framed as a follow-up to the May 2026 Mojo 1.0 beta article and the June 2026 Qualcomm-acquisition article, both cross-linked and verified to resolve.
concerns: Two quotes do not match their cited sources verbatim: the Pointer/UnsafePointer quote merges two adjacent sentences, and The Register quote attributes a 'Hacker News' detail that does not appear in that source at all. Both are documented in the corrections record filed alongside this review.
recommendations: Added modular.com, forum.modular.com, and mojolang.org to config/source_allowlist.txt -- all are Modular's own official domains (company blog, community forum, and the Mojo language's own site), used here as legitimate first-party sources for the company's own release.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Approve with corrections. The article is substantively accurate and well-sourced; two subordinate-claim quote-fidelity issues (not in the headline/summary/lead) are honestly covered by a public corrections note rather than requiring rejection.
editor_notes.duplicate_note: This submission is one of three independently-written articles covering the same Mojo 1.0 release (also PR #2200 and PR #2201). This one has the broadest sourcing (6 sources, including Modular's official forum) and is being approved as the canonical article; the other two should be reviewed against this one for rejection as duplicates once this merges.
